beats.text: OpenAI claims its AI just settled an old question about pi.
Pi never ends, so we guess it with a fraction. Twenty-two sevenths: close, not exact.
Three fifty-five over one thirteen: six decimals right, from tiny numbers.
Is pi secretly almost a fraction? Do fractions keep landing this close, forever?
Give each fraction a closeness score. Two is normal. Anything higher is luck.
Twenty-two sevenths: three point four. Three fifty-five over one thirteen: three point two. After that: about two.
Some numbers do hide behind fractions. This made-up one's score climbs forever.
OpenAI claims pi isn't like that. Past some size, no fraction scores above two.
Two is the lowest score possible. So pi is as far from a fraction as it gets.
Big if. Outside mathematicians haven't checked OpenAI's claim yet. Its computer-checkable proof files are public; we haven't checked those either.
